Subject: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming cadence requirements — Acme Retail

Hi Maya / Jared —

Great talking earlier — thanks for walking us through the primary integration and customer-facing use cases. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the performance / SLO items we agreed to qualify and next steps so we have alignment before the perf lab: 

Summary of stated targets (please correct if I've misstated):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 150 ms end-to-end for a standard access path (auth, routing, model warm). This is the hard SLO for the UI experience.
- Streaming: client expects server-initiated chunking (SSE or WebSocket) with first chunk within TTFT target and subsequent chunk cadence ~ every 250-400 ms for interactive responses (or after ~64 tokens).
- Throughput / concurrency: typical steady-state ~200 concurrent active users, peak ~600 concurrent sessions; expected peak request rate ~350 req/s with average response size ~150-300 tokens.
- Concurrency per connection: up to 6 simultaneous streams per user session (chat + background features).

What Redwood will validate in the perf lab:
1) End-to-end TTFT measured from client (browser) to first byte for both SSE and WebSocket transports.
2) Sustained chunk cadence under load (percentile distribution of inter-chunk gaps, target p95 <= 400 ms).
3) Throughput vs latency curve for your expected reply sizes and concurrency (we'll run step-load tests up to 2x your projected peak).
4) Resource footprint & recommended deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated), plus a preliminary cost estimate and quantization suggestions if needed.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO template and our streaming ops deck for context.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the TTFT requirement (150 ms) and whether the cadence constraint is a hard requirement or a preference?
- Please share any client-side instrumentation you can provide (browser traces / network HARs) so we can measure identically.
- Proposed: Redwood runs a 2-hour perf lab next Wed (Mar 25) — would that work?

I'll loop in Rishi (runtime) and Dev (solutions) on the lab.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: 150 ms is our bar for the initial token on the primary product page (desktop + mobile). For fallback experiences (batch generation), 300 ms is acceptable. So yes, 150 ms is hard for the default UI path.
- Cadence: the 250-400 ms cadence is preferred for the main chat flow; for some telemetry-heavy features we can accept up to 800 ms. So it's a soft requirement except for the main chat where we want p95 < 400 ms.
- Concurrent streams: we expect up to 4 simultaneous streams per active user, not 6 — apologies, earlier I overestimated.

Attached our internal SLO matrix (acme_slo-requirements.pdf) and a sample HAR from the desktop flow.

Thanks — can you also confirm whether Redwood supports both SSE and WebSocket natively and whether there are differences in TTFT or per-connection overhead?

Best,
Maya Singh

maya@acme-retail.com

Hi Maya — thanks for the clarification and for the SLO matrix + HAR. Quick notes from an infra/runtime perspective: 

SSE vs WebSocket support:
- Redwood supports both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming.
- In our experience TTFT differences are typically < 10-20 ms when comparing the two for identical network paths; the bigger drivers are connection warmup, route/path latency, and model forward time.
- WebSocket gives a bit more flexibility for bi-directional control messages, but SSE is simpler for browser-only flows. We'll test both.

TTFT tuning levers we plan to test:
- Keep-alive & connection pooling at the edge (reduce connection setup time).
- Pre-warmed model instances / small warm pool to avoid cold-starts for the primary UI path.
- Kernel & prompt compilation caching on the GPU side (important for quantized weights).
- Chunk generation policy: emit first chunk after model's first token output; for subsequent chunks we can tune cadences to your 250-400 ms target by adjusting decoding step batching.

Proposed perf lab plan (high level):
1) Baseline measurement using your HAR to reproduce client timings (measure TTFT across p50/p95/p99).
2) Transport comparison: SSE vs WebSocket (single connection) — measure overhead and per-connection CPU.
3) Scale tests: step load from 50 to 700 concurrent sessions with target reply sizes, measure TTFT & chunk cadence distributions.
4) Report: provide a short deck with measured curves, recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated), and configuration (batch sizes, KV cache policy, quantization levels).

We recommend Dedicated (reserved pool) if you need strict p95 TTFT guarantees at your projected peaks; Redwood Dedicated gives control over warm pools and lower multi-tenant jitter. We'll include a cost delta in the report.

Would you be able to open a temporary test account for us (or share a short-lived API key) so we can run the HAR-driven baseline from your network path? If not, we can run the same tests from our US-West lab but will note the path differences.

I'll prepare an instrumentation checklist and a short load script (k6 + custom SSE client) — attaching the initial ops deck for reference.

-Rishi
